\frac{\log_k(5^{k^2-1})}{\log_{k+1}(5^{k^2-4})}
= \frac{k^2-1}{k^2-4}\cdot \frac{\ln(k+1)}{\ln k}.
\]
So the product becomes
\[
\left(\prod_{k=4}^{63}\frac{k^2-1}{k^2-4}\right)
\left(\prod_{k=4}^{63}\frac{\ln(k+1)}{\ln k}\right).
\]
The log product telescopes:
\[
\prod_{k=4}^{63}\frac{\ln(k+1)}{\ln k}=\frac{\ln 64}{\ln 4}=3.
\]
Now compute the rational product:
\[
\prod_{k=4}^{63}\frac{k^2-1}{k^2-4}
=\prod_{k=4}^{63}\frac{(k-1)(k+1)}{(k-2)(k+2)}
=\frac{31}{13}.
\]
Thus the total product is
\[
3\cdot \frac{31}{13}=\frac{93}{13}.
\]
So \(m=93,\ n=13\), and
\[
m+n=106.
\]
